ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows a transition-state diagram with arrows that should be disregarded. On the left is a six-membered ring bearing two carbonyl C=O groups and an R1 substituent. On the right is an alkene/enamine-like component with a C=C bond, an H on the upper alkene carbon, an HN-R2 group attached to the lower alkene carbon, a methyl substituent, and an ester group labeled CO2R3. Reasoning: Following the assigned counting method and excluding all bonds involving hydrogen, first count the left component. The six-membered ring contributes 6 ring bonds. The two carbonyl groups contribute 2 C=O bonds. The attachment from the ring to R1 contributes 1 bond. Thus the left component has 6 + 2 + 1 = 9 non-H bonds. Next count the right component: the C=C bond contributes 1, the C-N bond contributes 1, the N-R2 bond contributes 1, the C-C bond from the alkene carbon to the ester carbonyl carbon contributes 1, the ester C=O bond contributes 1, the ester C-O bond contributes 1, the O-R3 bond contributes 1, and the C-C bond to the methyl substituent contributes 1. This gives 8 non-H bonds on the right. Adding both components gives 9 + 8 = 17.
